standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the bivariant class attached to the inclusion of the divisor and identifies the composite of pushforward with it as the first Chern class of the divisor's sheaf.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pushforward of bivariant classes and the definition of a bivariant class
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-push-proper-bivariant, invoked at proof line 6403
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes sense of the composite of a pushforward with a bivariant class, which is what allows the product of the Chern classes to be rewritten as a pushforward of a product on the divisor.

core_obligations: Reduce the last invertible sheaf to an effective Cartier divisor: by the quasi-projective case every invertible sheaf is the difference of the sheaves of two effective Cartier divisors, and since capping with a first Chern class is additive it suffices to treat the case where the last invertible sheaf is the sheaf of one effective Cartier divisor (proof lines 6385-6395).

Rewrite the product through the Gysin class of the divisor: with i the inclusion of the divisor and i^* its bivariant Gysin class, the composite of pushforward with i^* is the first Chern class of the sheaf of the divisor, and since the other Chern classes commute with both operations the product of d + 1 Chern classes equals the pushforward of the product of the first d restricted classes with i^* (proof lines 6397-6413).

Conclude by induction: the divisor has dimension strictly smaller than d because none of the generic points of X lie on it, so the induction hypothesis applies to the product of the d restricted Chern classes on D, and its pushforward vanishes (proof lines 6414-6415).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the last sheaf being the sheaf of an effective Cartier divisor (proof lines 6385-6395).
Factor the product through the Gysin class of the divisor (proof lines 6397-6413).
Apply the induction hypothesis on the divisor and push forward (proof lines 6414-6415).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that on a finite type scheme with an ample invertible sheaf and finite dimension d, the product of d + 1 first Chern classes vanishes in the bivariant group in degree d + 1 (statement lines 6373-6383, tag 0FDX). The proof runs an induction on the dimension: it reduces the last invertible sheaf to the sheaf of an effective Cartier divisor, rewrites the whole product as the pushforward of a product of the first d classes restricted to the divisor composed with the Gysin bivariant class, and concludes because the divisor has strictly smaller dimension. The rewriting through the Gysin class is the substance, so the claim is H2.
